preconditions.description: The integer n represents the length of the grid paths and must be between 2 and 1,000,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(path1) == n - 1 and all(c in {'N', 'E', 'S', 'W'} for c in path1)
preconditions.description: The first grid path is a string of length n-1, where each character is one of 'N', 'E', 'S', or 'W'.

preconditions.expression: len(path2) == n - 1 and all(c in {'N', 'E', 'S', 'W'} for c in path2)
preconditions.description: The second grid path is a string of length n-1, where each character is one of 'N', 'E', 'S', or 'W'.

preconditions.expression: not any(path1[i] == path1[i+1] and path1[i+1] == path1[i+2] and path1[i] != path1[i+2] for i in range(len(path1) - 2))
preconditions.description: The first grid path does not contain an alternating sequence of three moves (e.g., 'NES' or 'SWS').

preconditions.expression: not any(path2[i] == path2[i+1] and path2[i+1] == path2[i+2] and path2[i] != path2[i+2] for i in range(len(path2) - 2))
preconditions.description: The second grid path does not contain an alternating sequence of three moves (e.g., 'NES' or 'SWS').

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' if (exists_sequence(path1, path2) == True) else stdout.strip() == 'NO'
postconditions.description: The output is 'YES' if there exists a sequence of moves that brings both marbles to the last square of their respective paths simultaneously, otherwise 'NO'.
